title: Configure a 7-in-1 flip-socket driver with its blue 3/8-inch socket at the tip and seat it on a 3/8-inch hex standoff
instruction: Rearrange the flip-socket nut driver so that all three socket barrels are stored on its shaft with the blue 3/8-inch socket at the working tip, seat that socket fully over the 3/8-inch hex standoff on the bracket with the handle resting in the cradle beside it, then let go and move both hands clear.
context: The blue 3/8-inch socket sits behind the small red/yellow barrel, its blue end facing the handle; barrels leave and enter only over the tip, so red/yellow comes off first, green/blue next, and red/yellow goes back before green/blue, which must first be turned end for end. Each barrel indexes on the shaft's hex (2.4 degrees of play) and slides on only held square and clocked; the blue socket passes the 9.53 mm standoff within 4 degrees of its flats, turned 15 degrees off level (its crown chamfer turns a free tool in from about 15), and only standing proud of the tip. General maintenance and repair workers (O*NET 49-9071.00, 1,621,800 employees: 'Assemble, install, or repair wiring, electrical or electronic components, pipe systems, plumbing, machinery, or equipment.') drive hex-head fasteners with flip-socket nut drivers such as the Klein Tools 32900, whose 'Sockets store on shaft in any order or orientation'.
setup: Positions in mm from the midpoint between the arm bases, x forward, y left, z up from the bench. A light grey silicone mat 420 x 350 x 4 mm. The driver (Klein Tools 32900 7-in-1 Impact Flip Socket with Handle) lies along y in a rubber-lined 120-degree V cradle 130 mm long centred at x = 245, y = 145.5 under its hex cushion grip, the shaft's axis 40 mm up, its tip at y = 6 pointing towards the bracket (-y). On the shaft from the tip: the red 1/4 / yellow 5/16 barrel (red end out), a 4 mm gap, the green 11/32 / blue 3/8 barrel (green end out), a 6.5 mm gap, the brown 7/16 / red 1/2 barrel. A charcoal steel L-bracket (base 90 x 70 mm centred at x = 245, y = -175) carries a 3/8-inch hex stainless standoff (RAF 2236-1032-SS) threaded 2 mm into its face at the shaft's height: 7.5 mm of hex proud, flats turned 15 degrees off level, near face at y = -141.25. An end cradle like the start one but 46 mm long, its V bottom 2.54 mm lower, centred at y = -32. Two stands of two thin rails 24 mm apart at x = 170, y = -30 and -75, a barrel's centre lying across them at the shaft's height. The seed fixes nothing: the layout is the same every trial.
scoring: 0 for good if at any step the driver or any socket barrel falls off the bench (its centre more than 30 mm below the bench top); benign contact with the mat, the stands or the cradles costs nothing. 0.25: during the trial the green/blue barrel is slid fully off the front of the shaft (both faces more than 1 mm outboard of the tip), which the red/yellow barrel blocks until it is off first. 0.5: 0.25 met, and at the end all three barrels sit on the shaft (each coaxial within 10 degrees and 2 mm, the plain part of its through-bore wholly between tip and grip nose), the green/blue barrel at the working tip with its blue end outboard within 15 degrees and its blue face no more than 3 mm short of the tip. 1.0: 0.5 met, and at the end the blue socket is seated on the standoff (its mouth 5 to 11 mm past the standoff's near face, axis within 5 degrees of the standoff's, centre within 2.5 mm of it, hex within 4.4 degrees of the standoff's flats: the fit's 3.9 degrees of play and 0.5), the driver level within 8 degrees, the handle down in the end cradle (its centre within 25 mm of the seated position and within 6 mm of the cradle's seat height), both grippers open to 60 per cent or more and every hull corner of both hands 50 mm or more from the tool, the barrels, the stands, the cradles and the bracket, held so for 2.0 s with the tool moving 3 mm at most.
run_limit: 4600 steps (230 s at 20 Hz), about 2.5 times the reference run's 92.8 s
reset_notes: About 1 minute: slide the three barrels back on the shaft in the start order and orientation (brown/red at the grip, then green/blue green end out, then red/yellow red end out at the tip) and lay the tool in the start cradle with its tip on the cradle's tick mark (y = 6).
fidelity: Rigid bodies in PhysX at Klein's 32900 sizes (178 mm, 38.1 mm grip, 1/4-inch hex shaft, 272 g) and estimates read from its photos; every hex an exact prism of boxes. The barrels ride the shaft by contact alone (no joint, weld or computed force), shaft friction 0.16 (estimate: lubricated steel), with lead-ins on the shaft's tip and the standoff's crown. The real tool's ball detent and magnet are not modelled: a barrel stays where it is put by friction alone.
